# hrc-general-comment-22-1993
- **URL:** https://hrlibrary.umn.edu/gencomm/hrcom22.htm (archived University of Minnesota Human Rights Library copy of CCPR/C/21/Rev.1/Add.4; compiled in HRI/GEN/1/Rev.1 at 35 (1994)) ; Refworld and OHCHR copies returned 403 · **Accessed:** 2026-09-16 · **For:** v1 drafting, claim C18
- **What it establishes:** Human Rights Committee, General Comment No. 22: Article 18 (48th session, 1993). Para. 1 notes non-derogability; para. 3 says freedom of thought and conscience are "protected unconditionally" and that "no one can be compelled to reveal his thoughts". The phrase "forum internum" does **not** appear in GC22; it is the scholarly/Strasbourg label for what para. 3 describes.
- **Key passages:** Para. 1: "The right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion (which includes the freedom to hold beliefs) in article 18.1 is far-reaching and profound; it encompasses freedom of thought on all matters, personal conviction and the commitment to religion or belief". / "this provision cannot be derogated from, even in time of public emergency, as stated in article 4.2 of the Covenant." Para. 3: "Article 18 distinguishes the freedom of thought, conscience, religion or belief from the freedom to manifest religion or belief. It does not permit any limitations whatsoever on the freedom of thought and conscience or on the freedom to have or adopt a religion or belief of one's choice. These freedoms are protected unconditionally, as is the right of everyone to hold opinions without interference in article 19.1. In accordance with articles 18.2 and 17, no one can be compelled to reveal his thoughts or adherence to a religion or belief."
- **Reliability:** Primary text via an archived academic mirror (site archived 2023-02-01). Wording matches the version quoted in A/76/380 para. 26 (fn 51), which gives me a second, official-document cross-check on the key sentence.
- **Relevance to this project:** C18; the "absolute / unconditional" framing of the inner forum.
